title: Fabrication of 3D Cardiac Microtissue Arrays using Human iPSC-Derived Cardiomyocytes, Cardiac Fibroblasts, and Endothelial Cells
protocol: Use 1x phosphate buffered saline (PBS) or Hanks balanced salt solution (HBSS) without calcium or magnesium for cell wash solution preparation.
Prepare differentiation Medium #1 by adding 10 mL of supplement (50x B27 plus insulin) to 500 mL of cardiomyocyte basal medium (RPMI 1640).
Prepare differentiation Medium #2 by adding 10 mL of supplement (50x B27 minus insulin) to 500 mL of cardiomyocyte basal medium (RPMI 1640).
Prepare purification Medium #3 by adding supplement (50x B27 plus insulin) to 500 mL of cardiomyocyte basal medium (RPMI 1640) minus glucose.
Prepare endothelial growth medium (EGM) with commercially available endothelial cell growth medium supplement kit.
Dilute bovine serum albumin (BSA) stock solution to 1:20 with rinsing solution for cell separation sorting buffer preparation.
Prepare cardiac fibroblast differentiation medium by combining fibroblast basal medium (DMEM-high glucose) and Serum-Free Fibroblast Life Factors kit.

Prepare filtered maintenance medium for cardiac microtissue fabrication and maintenance using a ratio of cardiomyocyte basal medium (RPMI 1640) with supplement (50x B27 plus insulin) to endothelial growth medium in 70/30 v/v%.
Prepare 200 µL aliquots of GSK3-beta inhibitor CHIR 99021 at 10 mM concentration in dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO).
Prepare 200 µL aliquots of Wnt inhibitor IWR-1-endo at 10 mM concentration in DMSO.
Prepare 200 µL aliquots of transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) inhibitor SB431542 at 10 mM concentration in DMSO.
Store the aliquots for cell differentiation inhibitors at -80°C for up to 1 year.
Prepare 100 µL aliquots of basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF) at a concentration of 20 µg/mL in 0.1% BSA solution.
Prepare 100 µL aliquots of vascular endothelial growth factor 165 (VEGF165) at a concentration of 50 µg/mL in 0.1% BSA solution.
Prepare 100 µL aliquots of bone morphogenetic protein 4 (BMP4) at a concentration of 20 µg/mL in 0.1% BSA solution.
Store the differentiation factors for human iPSC-ECs at -80°C for up to 1 year.
Dilute Growth Factor Reduced basement membrane matrix medium in DMEM/F12 in a 1:200 ratio.
Add 2 mL of diluted basement membrane matrix medium to each well of the 6-well plate.
Leave the coated plates to set for at least 2 to 4 hours.
Liquefy 2% gelatin solution in a water bath at 37 °C.
Prepare filtered 0.2% (v/v) gelatin in PBS.
Coat the culture plate with 10 mL of 0.2% gelatin for at least 30 min at 37 °C prior to use.
Sterilize the 2% low melting agarose solution in PBS by autoclaving at 121 °C, 15 psi for 20 min.
Autoclave the casting silicone micro-molds at 121 °C, 15 psi for 15 min.
Prepare an enzyme digestion buffer of Dispase I (1 U/mL) and Liberase (3 U/mL) in PBS on ice.
Use ice cold commercially available fixation reagent containing 4.2% paraformaldehyde (PFA) for both cell and microtissue fixation.
Prepare 0.25% Triton X-100 in PBS for permeabilization.
Prepare 0.1% Tween-20 for washes, which can be stored at room temperature.
Prepare FACS buffer [PBS or HBSS with 2% fetal bovine serum (FBS)] and store at 4 °C.
Prepare 2% normal goat/donkey/rabbit serum in PBS based on the host species of raised antibodies.
Maintain iPSCs at approximately 75% to 80% confluency prior to cardiomyocyte differentiation.
Wash iPSC colonies once with 2 ml PBS after removing the culture medium from a 6-well plate.
On day 0, add 2 ml of differentiation Medium #1 containing CHIR (final concentration between 6-9 µM) to each well for mesendoderm induction.
On day 2, replace the medium in each well with fresh 2 ml of Medium #1.
On day 3, change the medium in each well to 2 ml of differentiation Medium #1 containing Wnt inhibitor IWR-1-endo (5 µM) to induce cardiac-lineage specification.
On day 5, replace the medium in each well with fresh 2 ml of Medium #1.
On day 7, switch the medium in each well to 2 ml of Medium #2.
Observe spontaneous beating of cardiomyocytes as early as day 8-9 or as late as day 11 for some lines.
On day 10, replace the medium with minus glucose Medium #3 in each well for purification of the differentiation culture.
Recover cells by changing the medium with 2 mL plus glucose Medium #2 on day 13.
Perform a second round of purification with 2 mL of Medium #3 in each well on day 16.
Recover the cells again on day 19 using 2 mL plus glucose Medium #2.
Wash the wells once with 1 mL PBS on day 20.
Dissociate the cells using 1 mL 10x Trypsin for 6 min at 37 °C.
Lift the cells off the well surface into single cells for less than 15 s and add to a 15 mL conical tube with equal volume of Medium #2 to neutralize the enzyme.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 3 min at 270 x g.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 3 mL Medium #3.
Count the cells and plate a total of ~3 million cells in each well of a new basement membrane matrix medium coated 6-well plate.
Replace the medium with fresh 2 mL Medium #2 on the second day after re-plating.
Replenish with 2 mL Medium #2 every other day until trypsinization for freezing or future experiments.
Wash the iPSC plate with PBS at 75% to 80% confluency.
Replace the medium with 2 mL of differentiation Medium #1 with 6 µM CHIR on day 0.
Replace the medium with 2 mL of differentiation Medium #1 with 2 µM CHIR on day 2.
Replace the medium with 2 mL of EGM supplemented with 20 ng bFGF-2, 50 ng VEGF165, and 20 ng BMP4 on day 4.
Change the medium with 2 mL of EGM supplemented with growth factors every 2 days from day 6 to day 10.
Add TGFβ inhibitor (SB431542) at 8 µM concentration to promote endothelial expansion and suppress differentiation on day 10.
Rinse each well with 1 mL of PBS on day 12.
Dissociate cells using 1 mL of 10x Trypsin for 8 min at 37 °C in a 6-well plate.
Neutralize the dissociation enzyme with an equal volume of EGM medium in a 50 mL conical tube.
Pass the cell suspension through a 40 µm cell strainer on the 50 mL conical tube, changing the filter for every 2 to 3 wells.
Enumerate total viable cells using 0.4% Trypan blue with a hemocytometer or automated cell counter.
Pellet the cell suspension at 300 x g for 5 min in a pre-cooled centrifuge set at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in appropriate volume of sorting buffer based on total count from step 3.8.
Add 80 µL of sorting buffer per 10^7 total cells.
Add 20 µL of FcR Blocking reagent per 10^7 cells, mix well, and incubate for 5 min.
Add 20 µL of CD144 or CD31 Microbeads per 10^7 cells, mix well, and incubate the cell suspension in dark at 4 °C for 15 min.
Wash the labeled cells with 20 mL of sorting buffer.
Pellet the cells at 300 x g for 5 min in a pre-cooled centrifuge set at 4 °C.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 3 mL of sorting buffer and leave it on ice.
Prepare a magnetic separation column by placing the column in the separator notch.
Rinse the column with 3 mL of sorting buffer and collect the flow through in a waste conical tube.
Thoroughly resuspend the cell suspension to break any clumps and apply it onto the column.
Wash the column with 3 mL of sorting buffer three times to remove unlabeled cells.
Place the column in a 15 mL conical tube for CD144+/CD31+ cell elution.
Add 5 mL of sorting buffer onto the column and immediately flush the magnetically labeled cells with the plunger.
Determine the viable cell number using 0.4% Trypan blue using a hemocytometer or an automated cell counter.
Centrifuge the cell suspension in a pre-cooled centrifuge at 300 x g for 3 min.
Resuspend the cell pellet in appropriate volume of EGM with 5-8 µM of TGFβ inhibitor (SB431542) based on the total count.
Plate passage 0 (P0) cells at an appropriate density (4 x 10^4 cells/cm²) on a pre-coated 0.2% gelatin plate.
Continue to replenish the medium with fresh EGM every 2 days with TGFβ inhibitor for P0 and P1.
From passage 2, culture cells in endothelial growth medium without TGFβ inhibitor.
Allow iPSCs to become 90% to 95% confluent.
Wash each well with 1 mL PBS.
Add 2 mL of differentiation Medium #1 with 11 µM CHIR on day 0.
Replace medium with 2 mL of cardiac fibroblast differentiation medium on day 4.
Disrupt the cell layer thoroughly and pass the cell suspension through a 70 μm cell strainer in a 50 mL conical tube containing equal volume of DMEM/F12 medium supplemented with 5% FBS on day 18.
Determine the viable cell number using 0.4% Trypan blue using a hemocytometer or an automated cell counter.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 x g for 5 min to obtain a pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in an appropriate volume of differentiation medium and plate at a cell density (6 x 10^4 cells/cm2) on a 0.2% gelatin coated plate until 90% confluency.
Melt agarose in a 100 mL glass bottle using a microwave until boiling.
Spray the melted agarose bottle and place it in the biosafety cabinet.
Allow the agarose to cool for approximately 3 minutes.
Pipette 700 µL of molten agarose into a silicone micro-mold with a 9 x 9 array, avoiding bubble formation.
Place the mold on a pre-cooled ice block to accelerate gelation.
Ensure that the agarose becomes translucent once gelled.
Carefully bend around the edges of the micro-mold to loosen the agarose replica.
Gently peel the replica from all sides to detach it from the silicone micro-mold.
Transfer the agarose microtissue tray containing 81 circular recesses (800 µm diameter; 750 µm depth) into a sterile 12-well plate.
Add 2 mL of PBS to the agarose microtissue tray and inspect under the microscope for any trapped bubbles or irregularly shaped wells.
Submerge the agarose tray in 2 mL of 70% ethanol overnight, followed by UV treatment in the biosafety cabinet for 1 hour.
Remove the 70% ethanol from the well and wash twice with distilled water.
Wash once more with 2 mL of PBS prior to use.
Trypsinize, neutralize, and count iPSC-CMs, iPSC-ECs, and iPSC-CFs.
Place the cell suspensions on ice.
Remove the PBS from the well and the cell seeding chamber carefully without touching the recesses.
Mix iPSC-CMs, iPSC-ECs, and iPSC-CFs in a 7:2:1 ratio to achieve a final cell density of 106 cells/mL.
Do not exceed 2 x 106 cells/mL.
Add the 200 µL of the cell suspension dropwise into the seeding chamber.
Allow the cells to settle at 37 °C in a CO2 incubator for 2 h.
Add microtissue fabrication medium surrounding the agarose mold to just cover the surface of the inner chamber.
Replace with fresh medium every 2 days for maintenance.
For each individual cell type, culture the cells separately on basement membrane matrix medium or gelatin coated chamber slides (approximately 2.5-3 x 105 cells/mL).
Cardiac microtissues can be collected in a 15 mL conical tube by gently flushing them out of the circular recesses.
Aspirate the medium and rinse the cells or microtissues with 1 mL PBS.
Fix with fixation buffer containing 4.2% PFA for 20 min for chamber slides and 1 h for microtissues at room temperature.
Aspirate the PFA and add 1 mL of permeabilizing solution (0.25% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 5 to 7 min for chamber slides and 20 min for microtissues in a 15 mL conical tube.
Aspirate the permeabilizing solution.
Rinse once with 2 to 3 mL of PBS.
Incubate the cells with 500-1,000 µL of blocking solution for at least 1 h for chamber slides and 3 to 4 h for microtissues.
Incubate the cells or cardiac microtissues with conjugated antibodies prepared in the blocking solution sufficient to cover the sample.
Incubate with anti-cardiac Troponin-T (cTnT2) (1:50), anti-CD31 (1:75), and anti-DDR2/Vimentin (1:50) for 1 h for chamber slides and overnight at 4 °C for cardiac microtissues.
Wash the chamber slides three times with 500 µL 0.1% Tween-20 for 5 min between each wash and a final wash with PBS.
For the cardiac microtissues, wash with 2 mL 0.1% Tween-20 five times with 20 min duration between each wash.
Perform a final wash step for an additional 20 min.
Incubate the cells or microtissues with 4',6-diamidino-2-phenylindole (DAPI) (1 µg/mL) prior to confocal microscopy.
For cardiac microtissues, transfer carefully to a 35 mm glass bottom dish and add PBS to submerge microtissues.
Gain center focus of the microtissue using a 20x or 40x oil immersion objective.
Adjust exposure parameters for each fluorophore.
Set first and last coordinates in Live mode with a total imaging depth of 100-200 µm with 5-10 µm slice interval.
Gently flush microtissues with Medium #1 using a wide-bore 1 mL pipette tip into a 15 mL conical tube.
Rinse cells or microtissues with 1 mL PBS and add 200-300 µL of enzyme digestion buffer for 20 min at 37 °C.
Mix the microtissues gently for 1 min at 10 min, then incubate again at 37 °C for the remainder of time.
Use a regular 1 mL pipette tip to mix the microtissues vigorously after incubation to obtain a turbid cell suspension.
Neutralize the cell suspension with 5 mL of medium containing 5% FBS once the microtissues are digested into single cells.
Strain the cell suspension through a 40 µm cell strainer and count the total number of cells.
Centrifuge the single cell suspension at 300 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend 1 x 10^5-1 x 10^6 cells in 100 µL annexin-binding buffer with FITC Annexin V and 100 µg/mL propidium iodide (PI) or To-Pro3.
Incubate the cell suspension for 10 min on ice.
Add 300 µL of the annexin binding buffer to the cell suspension after incubation.
Transfer the cell suspension to a round bottom FACS tube for flow cytometry analysis.
Prepare fixed cells by performing fixation as described in steps 6.2.
Permeabilize the cell pellet according to step 6.3 instructions.
Rinse the permeabilized cell pellet thoroughly.
Incubate cells with respective conjugated antibodies for 1 hour.
Wash the cell pellet twice in 4 mL FACS buffer by centrifuging at 300 x g for 3 min each time.
Resuspend the washed cells in 200-300 μL FACS buffer for flow cytometry analysis.
Adjust forward and side scatter properties using an unstained sample.
Use isotype controls for each fluorophore to adjust laser voltages if necessary.
Collect a minimum of 20,000 events for data analysis.
Record videos of cardiac microtissues capturing at least three beats.
Set the recording resolution to at least 1280 x 720 pixels with frame rate >30 frames per second.
Save video in .AVI format.
Run MotionGUI script in a MATLAB environment.
Locate and load the .AVI file from your folder into the user interface.
Enter the frame rate used for capturing the video in the Input panel.
Specify pixel size based on resolution and capture magnification in the advanced input panel if applicable.
Set a suitable macroblock pixel size (default 16) and detectable pixel motion according to contraction strength.
Click on Get Motion Vectors to begin the analysis.
Select a region of interest using the Choose AOI radio button.
Use Map Time Ave to generate a mean contraction heatmap based on detected motion on X and Y axes.
Use Get Contraction Data to automatically measure contraction and relaxation peaks.
Apply peak height and distance thresholds for maximum contraction velocity (blue dot) and maximum relaxation velocity (red triangle).
Select Analyze Peaks to obtain contraction, relaxation values, beat rate, and beat interval measurements.
Obtain measurements from a minimum of 25 individual microtissues for statistical analyses.
